name: Mechanical Wear and Switching Counters
description: The system thinks about the equipment's operating life, not just its current state. A series of switching cycles runs the counter up to a (temporarily lowered, for this short demo) warning threshold, which raises a signal - the natural moment to show the Service History tab.

steps.description: Temporarily lowers DI1's switching-counter warning threshold to 3 cycles, just for this demo - the real threshold (and every other counter value) is restored the moment the presentation stops, exactly like every tag it touches.
Cycle 3: close - this reaches the (lowered) warning threshold

steps.message: DI1's switching counter has reached its warning threshold (3 cycles) - mechanical wear review recommended
steps.description: See Digital Inputs > Switching Counter for DI1 - now at/over threshold

This scenario deliberately never adds a service note itself - service-history entries are permanent and cannot be edited or deleted (by design), so a note written by a demo would stay in the device's real history forever. This is the natural point to show the Service History tab live and, if you want to, add a real note as the presenter.
